Rook smiles. His hand twitches towards his breast pocket, as if he wanted to hide something.

Someday we'll see her again. I hope we'll recognise her then.

The Rust Brothers. Price is right.

Dr. Fenwick, Polizeiarzt. Wenn Sie nicht: Dr. Fenwick, police surgeon. If you're not bleeding, keep it short.

Edmund Thorne sits downstairs. His lawyer has three witnesses from Anchor Yard who swear he was there all night. I'm afraid we have the wrong man.

And the file stays open, whether it's closed or not.

Vey. I haven't heard that name in twelve years.

“Greta's gift. I had to pawn it when money was short. That's why I got involved with that woman, with Vey ... Thank you. Take this, it's no use to me any more.”

And the bell in the tower ... Price swears he heard it strike by itself. Vey is still out there, and now she has what she wanted.

(End of case 4. Talk to Marlowe again.)

Good that you're here. Read this.

Madame Odile Varenne, the diva of the Lumen Theatre at the North Gate, lost her voice in the middle of the second act. Just like that. And the same night the tower clock at the North Gate stopped at 3:33. Since then it strikes three notes at night.

Price already has a suspect, the mute mask maker. That's too convenient for me. Three notes, investigator. You know whose song that is.

We didn't find Hester Marsh. But Dr. Fenwick examined the crypt and found fibres that don't belong there. Police cloth.

One of us helped Vey. I can't trust anyone here. Except you, perhaps. Find out who it was, and where that choir has disappeared to. Quietly.

Hester Marsh woke up this morning. Dr. Fenwick is with her, over in the infirmary.

She says a man in a police coat carried her into the crypt. A policeman. One of us.

I can't trust anyone here. Except you, perhaps. Find out who it was, and where that choir has disappeared to. Quietly.

I don't know if I can believe you again. Prove it to me.

“Grimes. I always suspected it and could never prove it.”

By evening the Old Market has a new market warden, and Greta gets her stall for free.

Holt rubs his eyes. “Someone wanted to pin that on me, eh? My wife is dying, and some swine writes notes in my name.”

“Listen: if it's Rook ... I trained him. After the third blow he drops his guard. Always. Remember that.”
Holt stellt sich breitbeinig hin. „Keine: Holt plants his feet wide. “Don't worry, I'll go easy.”
Holt. Ich hab ihn nachts im Keller geseh: Holt. I saw him in the cellar at night, with a letter. Don't tell anyone, he's my superior.

Here. Both nights. Until morning. Signed by the head nurse. Who says otherwise?
I'll go to the North Gate.
I'll go to the counting house.
I think this belongs to you.

She meant her daughter Lilian.

I know what happened to Hester.
I know who the mole is.
I know who the thirteenth guest is.
I know who is stealing the voices.

I know where the bell hangs.

Your reputation. Solve cases cleanly, catch crooks, and doors open: files, witnesses, my patience. Accuse innocent people, and you're back on the street.

And one more thing: a statement is only an assumption. Only when a second source says the same do I believe it.

That doesn't make it better. But it explains something.

(End of case 6. Talk to Marlowe again.)

And on every new photo plate in the city there is one guest too many.

“Price will seal off the canal. You go down into the chamber. And investigator: this time she doesn't escape us.”

Marlowe sieht dich lange an. Dann unters: Marlowe looks at you for a long time. Then she signs a manhunt order.

Marlowe sieht dich lange an. „Wie Sie me: Marlowe looks at you for a long time. “As you wish.”

Marlowe doesn't look up from the file. “Thorne is filed away. And you're standing around here.

Little Kettle from the Night Market asked for you again today. For the third time. Orphans walking about at night, a boy who's missing. I have no constable to spare for it, and Price laughs at her.

Go to the Night Market and hear what she has to say. You'll only get the next case from me once that's done.”

Marlowe looks up from her files and isn't even startled. “You shouldn't be here at all. Price is hanging your face on every lantern.”

She slides a cup of tea over to you. “Drink up and go out through the yard. And write to me from Wexmoor. No sender.”

(End of chapter 1. Kettlegate stays open for side tasks.)

Marlowe stands at the window and waves you over without turning around. “See that one? Next to the church tower.”

A star. In the middle of the day.

“Professor Starling from the observatory has been missing for three nights. Price thinks he was abducted.” She turns around and puts an envelope into her drawer. “And this came for Price today. No sender. It's about you.”

Marlowe stands up and buttons her coat. “Two cases, one woman. Price seals off Ashgrove, and nobody drinks tea tonight.”

“Go into the cellar. And investigator: bring me the boy.”
Marlowe steht auf und nimmt ihren Mantel:

“Price will close off the theatre. You go up through the tower. And investigator: bring the voices back if you can. Not just the man.”

“Price is waiting at the Canal Harbour with two men. You go first, you know the case better than any of us. And take something to bandage with.”

She waits until you look up. “In his armchair. In a bolted room. With dry clothes. Price wants to see the nephew hang, he inherits everything.

Oh, and little Kettle from the Night Market asked for you twice. Something about orphans. I told her you're busy.”
Marlowe zieht die Schublade wieder auf u: Marlowe opens the drawer again and reads aloud without looking at you.
Mehr noch: Vey wollte mit Hesters Leben: More than that: Vey wanted to bring back her daughter Lilian with Hester's life. I destroyed the music box.

The seven women are home. They sing again, they say in Ashgrove. Good work, investigator.

(End of case 5. Talk to Marlowe again.)
Miriam Vey, unter fremdem Gesicht. Sie h: Miriam Vey, under a stranger's face. She cast the voices into a bell, and it will strike at the new moon beneath the foundry.
Miriam Vey. The choir never stopped.
Miss Pimm nimmt das Buch mit zwei Finger: Miss Pimm takes the book with two fingers, as if it were wet, and locks it in a lead box. “Unopened. Good. Some things should just stay on the shelf.”
Miss Wren führt die Kinder an Traumfäden: Miss Wren leads the children on dream threads. Benji brought Thorne the water in his sleep, because Thorne wanted to evict St. Brigid.
Miss Wren vergiftet die Kinder mit ihrem: Miss Wren poisons the children with her tea.

Moll? Hat mir beim Würfeln letzte Woche: Moll? Paid me in silver at dice last week. Silver with a funny eye on it. A gravedigger with silver, I ask you.
One more thing: keep your eyes open. Whoever works against Vey here has been sleeping badly lately. And whoever works for her doesn't sleep at all.

Pell is free again. He wrote on his slate that he forgives you. I don't know if I can.

The tower clock sings every night. And every week a singer loses her voice.

(End of case 4. Talk to Marlowe again.)

Since then children nobody knows stand in the windows. They wave.

(End of case 5. Talk to Marlowe again.)

If you're not afraid of vermin: back left, behind the last shelf.

Rook. A boy I hired myself. I should have seen it.

Vey is still out there somewhere. But Kettlegate sleeps a little easier tonight. Thanks to you.

Rook? Neu hier. Kam vor einem halben Jah: Rook? New here. Came from the old chapel parish of St. Ebba half a year ago. Hard-working, always the first in and the last out. Why do you ask?

She lowers her voice. “The hymnal of the hospital choir. Confiscated in St. Ebba, evidence number 112. Last week the shelf was empty and the seal lay on the floor.

Silver candlesticks from St. Ebba, the report says. Never seen the things! The young constable nabbed me when I was taking a leak by the ruins at night. Just put the candlesticks down at my feet.

Ask the sexton. Ask anyone. I'm many things, but no church thief.

Later. There's news: Hester Marsh, fourteen, has disappeared. The same morning the sexton of St. Ebba found an opened child's grave.

Constable Rook thinks the girl simply ran away. Check that.

When someone winds up, you see a ring coming at you. Space, and you dodge. That almost always works. F, and you parry. That's harder, the window is narrow. But whoever parries gathers focus and strikes back right away. Whoever parries every blow sets up a counterattack.

And when you strike yourself: press at the right moment, then it lands properly. You need focus for skills. Show me.

Get some rest, investigator. The next case will come soon enough.

„Ein Professor, der Sterne erntet.“ Marl: “A professor who harvests stars.” Marlowe rubs her eyes. “If I take that to the commissioner, he'll arrest us both. Two sources for the harvest, two for the night. Then I'll come along.”
